title: Kurtz et al. 2020, Environmental Science & Technology 54(19): 12434-12446, "Mapping U.S. Food System Localization Potential: The Impact of Diet on Foodsheds"
what_taken: 378 US metros, 3,106 counties, 7 diets, 3 land types (Peters 2016 Foodprint with county productivity); county HNEs called county carrying capacity (eq 2). National average weighted source distance 351-481 km cultivated cropland, 80-492 km perennial, 117-799 km grazing (Table 2; the abstract's 351-428 omits the baseline diet at 481). Within 250 km, 35-53% of the metro population on cultivated cropland, 39-94% perennial, 26-88% grazing (Fig. 5). Land per person a year by diet (Fig. 2): baseline 1.248 ha (0.965 of it grazing), vegan 0.136 ha. Every diet leaves land unused.
notes: Full text read (archive copy, 13 pp.). Method family: resource-based land and diet with spatial allocation (foodshed), the same label as Peters 2009 (B20's 'land per diet' is the HALF-type family, so not that). The 35-53% is of the aggregate metro population, not all people. Grazing is 77% of the baseline footprint; compare B202 (Peters 2016, 1.08 ha, national average yields; Kurtz is county-weighted). Diets: baseline 2,844 kcal, others about 2,150 kcal. 1,571 of 3,106 counties meet their own cultivated-cropland need on the baseline diet but hold only 17.6% of the population. Its comparison with Zumkehr and Campbell (p. 12442) is consistent with that paper. Lane: not cited.
